pages.title: Life Cycle Coloring Book Prompts: Butterfly, Frog, Chicken & Plant
pages.metaDescription: Life cycle coloring book prompts for kids: butterfly, frog, chicken and plant life cycles, one stage per page with a short fact to read and color.
pages.intro: Life cycles are on almost every early science curriculum, and coloring each stage helps kids remember the order. These life cycle coloring book prompts give one stage per page with a short, accurate caption, from a monarch egg on a milkweed leaf to a seed carried off by the wind. They suit teachers, homeschoolers and parents of curious kids aged 3 to 13.
tips: List the stages in order in the brief; one stage becomes one page, so the page count is the number of stages.
Use the real vocabulary (chrysalis, tadpole, germination) and the book does the teaching while kids color.
End on the stage that starts the cycle again, so kids see that it is a circle, not a line.

prompts.name: Butterfly life cycle for preschoolers

fields.description: How a monarch caterpillar becomes a butterfly, one simple step per page: 1. A butterfly lays a tiny egg on a milkweed leaf. 2. A small caterpillar hatches and eats its eggshell. 3. It munches milkweed leaves all day. 4. It grows so fast it sheds its skin. 5. It hangs upside down in a J shape. 6. It makes a green chrysalis. 7. Inside, its body changes. 8. A butterfly comes out. 9. It dries its wings in the sun. 10. It drinks flower nectar and lays eggs of its own.

prompts.why: Preschool teachers run a butterfly unit every spring, and ten big, simple stages with one short sentence each are just right for a four-year-old. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Frog and chicken life cycles

fields.description: Two life cycles, seven stages each. Frog: 1. Frogspawn, eggs in jelly in a pond. 2. A tadpole hatches and breathes with gills. 3. It swims and eats algae. 4. Back legs grow. 5. Front legs grow. 6. A froglet with a short tail climbs out. 7. An adult frog breathes air and eats insects. Chicken: 8. A hen lays an egg. 9. She keeps it warm for about 21 days. 10. The chick pecks through the shell. 11. The wet chick dries fluffy. 12. Feathers grow in. 13. A young hen scratches for seeds. 14. The grown hen lays eggs.

prompts.why: Comparing a frog's change in water with a chick's growth in an egg is a standard grade 1-3 lesson, and teachers can use both halves for a compare-and-contrast activity. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Flowering plant life cycle in depth

fields.description: The life cycle of a flowering plant: 1. A seed: seed coat, embryo and stored food. 2. Germination needs water, air and warmth. 3. The root grows down first. 4. The shoot pushes up and the seed leaves (cotyledons) open. 5. True leaves make food by photosynthesis. 6. The grown plant forms a bud. 7. The flower's parts: petals, stamens, pistil. 8. Pollination by insects or wind. 9. Fertilization in the ovary. 10. Seeds form inside a fruit. 11. Seeds spread by wind, water and animals. 12. A seed waits in the soil to start again.

prompts.why: Homeschoolers and grade 4-6 teachers need the right vocabulary (cotyledon, stamen, fertilization) with a picture to anchor each word. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Solar System Coloring Book Prompts: Planets, Moon & Space Facts
pages.metaDescription: Solar system coloring book prompts for kids: the Sun, all eight planets, moon phases and eclipses, one fact per page to color and learn.
pages.intro: A solar system coloring book turns planet facts into something kids can hold, color and remember. These prompts go from a simple Sun-and-planets tour for preschoolers to orbits, seasons and eclipses for 9 to 13 year olds. Every fact is checked and kept short, so the book works for a classroom space unit or a homeschool science week.
tips: Keep the planets in order from the Sun in the brief; kids learn the order by turning the pages.
Give each planet one memorable fact (Jupiter is the biggest, Venus is the hottest) rather than a paragraph.
Mention that Pluto is a dwarf planet; teachers check for that.

prompts.name: Sun, Moon and planets for little learners

fields.description: A first trip through our solar system, one stop per page: 1. The Sun is a star that gives us light and warmth. 2. Mercury is closest to the Sun and the smallest planet. 3. Venus is the hottest planet. 4. Earth is our home, with oceans and air. 5. The Moon goes around Earth. 6. Mars is the red planet. 7. Jupiter is the biggest planet. 8. Saturn has bright rings of ice and rock. 9. Uranus spins on its side. 10. Neptune is cold, blue and very windy.

prompts.why: Parents and preschool teachers want a gentle first space book with one easy fact per planet, in the right order from the Sun. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Planets and space neighbors for ages 6-9

fields.description: Our solar system for early readers: 1. The Sun, the star at the center. 2. Planets travel around the Sun in orbits. 3. Mercury. 4. Venus. 5. Earth. 6. The Moon has craters. 7. Moon phases. 8. Mars and its rovers. 9. The asteroid belt. 10. Jupiter and its Great Red Spot storm. 11. Saturn's rings. 12. Uranus. 13. Neptune. 14. Pluto, a dwarf planet. 15. Comets have tails that point away from the Sun. 16. Astronauts explore space. Give each planet one fact: size, color, or how hot or cold it is.

prompts.why: Grade 1-3 teachers can use one page a day during a space unit, and the moon phases and comet pages add facts beyond the planet list. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: How the solar system works for ages 9-13

fields.description: How the solar system works, for upper elementary: 1. Gravity holds the planets in orbit around the Sun. 2. Earth spins once a day. 3. Earth orbits the Sun once a year. 4. Seasons come from Earth's tilted axis. 5. Moon phases. 6. Solar eclipse. 7. Lunar eclipse. 8. Rocky inner planets. 9. Gas and ice giants. 10. The asteroid belt. 11. Jupiter's moons. 12. Saturn's rings are pieces of ice and rock. 13. The Kuiper Belt and dwarf planets. 14. Comets. 15. Telescopes. 16. Rovers and probes explore other worlds.

prompts.why: Homeschoolers and middle-grade teachers need the 'why' behind seasons, phases and eclipses, and a labeled picture of each makes the idea stick. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Water Cycle and Weather Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Water cycle and weather coloring book prompts for kids: evaporation, clouds, rain, snow, rainbows and seasons, one idea per page with a short fact.
pages.intro: The water cycle and weather are early science staples, and kids understand evaporation better once they have colored the Sun warming a puddle. These prompts cover a simple rain story for preschoolers, a weather book for 6 to 9 year olds and an in-depth water cycle book with real vocabulary for older kids. Each page holds one idea and one short caption.
tips: Write the cycle as a sequence of steps so the pages follow the water from the sea, up to the clouds and back.
Use the four key words, evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection, from age 6 up.
For weather books, pair each kind of weather with what you wear or do in it; young kids remember the umbrella.

prompts.name: Where does rain come from

fields.description: A simple water cycle story for little kids: 1. The Sun warms the water in the sea, lakes and puddles. 2. Tiny bits of water rise into the air where we cannot see them. 3. High up, the air is cold and the water makes clouds. 4. The clouds get full and heavy. 5. Rain falls down. 6. When it is very cold, snow falls instead. 7. Rain makes puddles, streams and rivers. 8. Rivers flow back to the sea. 9. Plants and animals drink the water. 10. The Sun warms the water again and the cycle goes round.

prompts.why: Preschool and kindergarten teachers want the water cycle as a simple circular story with no hard words, and ten steps fit a two-week weather unit. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Weather and seasons for ages 6-9

fields.description: Kinds of weather and how we measure them: 1. Sunny. 2. Cloudy. 3. Rainy. 4. Windy. 5. Snowy: snowflakes have six sides. 6. Foggy: a cloud near the ground. 7. Thunderstorms: we see lightning before we hear thunder. 8. Rainbows: sunlight shining through raindrops. 9. Hail: balls of ice from storm clouds. 10. Spring. 11. Summer. 12. Fall. 13. Winter. 14. Weather tools: a thermometer, a rain gauge and a wind vane. Show a child dressed right for each weather; for thunderstorms and hail, show the child safely indoors at the window.

prompts.why: Grade 1-2 teachers cover weather types, seasons and tools in one unit, and this book matches that outline page for page. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: The water cycle in depth for ages 9-13

fields.description: The water cycle with real science words: 1. Most of Earth's water is salty ocean; only about 3% is fresh. 2. Evaporation: the Sun turns water into vapor. 3. Transpiration: plants release water through their leaves. 4. Condensation: vapor cools into droplets and forms clouds. 5. Cloud types: cumulus, stratus, cirrus, cumulonimbus. 6. Precipitation: rain, snow, sleet, hail. 7. Runoff into streams. 8. Infiltration into soil. 9. Groundwater and aquifers. 10. Glaciers and ice caps store fresh water. 11. Water treatment. 12. Saving water.

prompts.why: Upper elementary teachers need evaporation, transpiration and infiltration taught as separate steps, and homeschoolers get a ready-made unit. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Human Body Coloring Book Prompts: Senses, Organs & Body Systems
pages.metaDescription: Human body coloring book prompts for kids: the five senses, heart, lungs, bones, brain and body systems, one idea per page with an easy fact.
pages.intro: Kids are endlessly curious about how their own bodies work, and coloring a heart or a skeleton makes anatomy friendly instead of gross. These human body coloring book prompts start with the five senses for preschoolers and build to full organ systems for 9 to 13 year olds. Every fact is short, accurate and age-appropriate.
keywords: human body coloring pages for kids
tips: For young kids, show a friendly child using each body part (smelling a flower, listening to a bell) rather than an anatomy chart.
Use one system per page for older kids; a page that tries to show everything gets cluttered.
End with healthy habits like sleep, water and washing hands, so the book closes on something kids can do.

prompts.name: My amazing body for preschoolers

fields.description: A first book about my body, one idea per page with a child doing something: 1. My eyes see colors. 2. My ears hear music. 3. My nose smells flowers. 4. My tongue tastes food. 5. My skin feels soft and rough things. 6. My heart beats to pump blood. 7. My lungs breathe in air. 8. My bones hold me up. 9. My muscles help me run and jump. 10. My tummy digests food. 11. My brain helps me think and learn. 12. I keep my body healthy: wash hands, eat fruit, sleep.

prompts.why: Preschool teachers cover 'my body' and the five senses every year, and showing a child using each part keeps it friendly for a 4-year-old. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: How my body works for ages 6-9

fields.description: How the body works for early readers: 1. Grown-ups have 206 bones. 2. The skull protects the brain. 3. Muscles pull on bones to move us. 4. The heart is a muscle about the size of your fist. 5. Blood travels in tubes called blood vessels. 6. Lungs fill with air when we breathe in. 7. Chewing starts digestion. 8. The stomach mixes food. 9. The intestines take in nutrients. 10. The brain sends messages along nerves. 11. Skin is the largest organ. 12. Kids have 20 baby teeth. 13. The five senses. 14. Sleep helps us grow.

prompts.why: Grade 1-3 teachers and homeschoolers get a fact a page that kids can repeat at dinner, which is how they remember it. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Body systems for ages 9-13

fields.description: The body's systems, one per page, with the main organs labeled: 1. Cells are the building blocks of life. 2. Skeletal system. 3. Muscular system. 4. Circulatory system: heart, arteries, veins. 5. Red blood cells carry oxygen. 6. Respiratory system: lungs and diaphragm. 7. Digestive system. 8. The liver and kidneys clean the blood. 9. Nervous system. 10. The brain's main parts. 11. The eye. 12. The ear. 13. Skin, hair and nails. 14. Immune system: white blood cells fight germs. 15. Teeth. 16. Exercise, sleep and food keep the systems strong.

prompts.why: Middle-grade science covers body systems one at a time, and a labeled coloring page per system works as a study aid before a test. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: How Plants Grow Coloring Book Prompts: Seeds, Roots & Photosynthesis
pages.metaDescription: How plants grow coloring book prompts for kids: seed to flower, what plants need, plant parts and photosynthesis, one idea per page to color.
pages.intro: Planting a seed is one of the first science experiments most kids do, and a coloring book helps them understand what is happening under the soil. These prompts go from a sunflower growing step by step for preschoolers to plant parts and photosynthesis for older kids. They pair beautifully with a real bean in a jar on the windowsill.
keywords: parts of a plant coloring page
tips: Show the soil cut away on some pages so kids can see roots growing underground.
Pair the book with a real seed in a clear cup; kids compare their plant to the page.
For older kids, name the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis exactly: sunlight, water and carbon dioxide in; sugar and oxygen out.

prompts.name: From seed to sunflower

fields.description: How a sunflower grows, one step per page with a child gardener: 1. We plant a seed in the soil. 2. We water it. 3. The Sun shines and warms the ground. 4. A tiny root grows down. 5. A sprout pushes up out of the soil. 6. Two small leaves open. 7. The stem grows tall, taller than me. 8. A big bud forms and follows the Sun across the sky. 9. The bud opens into a bright sunflower facing the morning Sun. 10. The flower makes new seeds for birds and for next year.

prompts.why: Parents and preschool teachers planting seeds in spring want a book that matches what the child sees in the cup, step by step. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: What plants need and plant parts

fields.description: What plants need and what each part does: 1. Plants need sunlight. 2. Plants need water. 3. Plants need air. 4. Plants need soil with nutrients. 5. Plants need space to grow. 6. Roots hold the plant and drink water. 7. The stem carries water up to the leaves. 8. Leaves make food for the plant. 9. Flowers make seeds. 10. Fruits protect seeds, like an apple or a tomato. 11. Some seeds we eat: peas, corn, beans. 12. Try it: grow a bean in a jar with a wet paper towel.

prompts.why: Grade 1-2 'plant needs and parts' units are universal, and the bean-in-a-jar page gives teachers a hands-on finish. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Photosynthesis and plant science for ages 9-13

fields.description: Plant science: 1. Plants make their own food. 2. Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. 3. It makes sugar and gives off oxygen. 4. Chlorophyll makes leaves green. 5. Stomata are tiny holes in leaves. 6. Xylem carries water up. 7. Phloem carries sugar around the plant. 8. Root hairs soak up water. 9. Plants grow toward light. 10. Roots grow down with gravity. 11. Fall leaves change color as chlorophyll fades. 12. Cactus stems store water. 13. Carnivorous plants catch insects. 14. Plants feed almost every food chain.

prompts.why: Teachers and homeschoolers need photosynthesis, xylem and phloem drawn clearly, and coloring each part helps kids learn the names. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Community Helpers Coloring Book Prompts for Preschool and Up
pages.metaDescription: Community helpers coloring book prompts for kids: firefighters, doctors, teachers, mail carriers and more, each with what they do and the tools they use.
pages.intro: Community helpers is a favorite preschool and kindergarten unit, and kids love coloring the firefighter's truck or the vet's stethoscope. These prompts give one helper per page with a sentence about what they do, then build to tools, vehicles and how a town's services connect for older kids. Show a mix of people of different backgrounds, ages and genders in every role.
tips: Ask for a diverse mix of people across the helpers; teachers want every child to see themselves in a job.
Give each helper a tool or vehicle in the picture; it is what kids recognize first.
For older kids, show how helpers depend on each other, like a 911 dispatcher sending the paramedics.

prompts.name: Community helpers for preschoolers

fields.description: People who help in our town, one per page with one easy sentence: 1. A firefighter puts out fires. 2. A police officer keeps us safe. 3. A doctor helps us when we are sick. 4. A nurse takes care of patients. 5. A teacher helps us learn. 6. A mail carrier brings letters. 7. A garbage collector keeps streets clean. 8. A farmer grows our food. 9. A baker makes bread. 10. A librarian helps us find books. 11. A dentist checks our teeth. 12. A crossing guard helps us cross the street. Show men and women of many backgrounds.

prompts.why: Community helpers is in nearly every pre-K curriculum, and teachers want one clear helper per page with a sentence a child can repeat. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Helpers, tools and vehicles for ages 6-9

fields.description: Community helpers with the tools and vehicles they use: 1. Firefighter: hose, ladder truck. 2. Paramedic: ambulance, stretcher. 3. Doctor: stethoscope. 4. Veterinarian: caring for a dog. 5. Teacher: whiteboard and books. 6. Mail carrier: mail truck. 7. Pilot: cockpit. 8. Bus driver. 9. Construction worker: hard hat and crane. 10. Electrician: wires and tools. 11. Plumber: wrench and pipes. 12. Farmer: tractor. 13. Chef: kitchen. 14. Librarian. 15. Sanitation worker: recycling truck. 16. Park ranger: trail map.

prompts.why: Grade 1-2 teachers extend the helpers unit to tools and vehicles, and kids who love trucks get a reason to color every page. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: How a community works for ages 9-13

fields.description: How a town works: 1. A 911 dispatcher answers emergency calls. 2. Firefighters and paramedics respond. 3. Doctors and nurses work in a hospital. 4. Water treatment workers clean our drinking water. 5. Line workers fix power lines. 6. Sanitation and recycling workers. 7. Road crews fix potholes. 8. Mail carriers. 9. Farmers and grocery workers bring food to town. 10. Teachers and librarians. 11. Town council members make local decisions. 12. Judges. 13. Volunteers at a food bank. 14. How kids can help their community.

prompts.why: Social studies teachers in grades 3-5 cover local government and public services, and this book connects jobs to how a community runs. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Recycling and Earth Day Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Recycling and Earth Day coloring book prompts for kids: sorting recycling, reduce reuse recycle, composting and saving energy, one idea per page.
pages.intro: Earth Day on April 22 brings a rush of teachers and parents looking for recycling activities that actually teach something. These prompts turn sorting, composting, saving water and the journey of a plastic bottle into one-idea-per-page coloring books. They work for a single Earth Day lesson or a whole green-habits unit.
keywords: earth day coloring pages for kids
tips: Publish or print in March; Earth Day searches peak in the weeks before April 22.
Keep the habits practical (turn off the tap while brushing) so kids can do them the same day.
Avoid scary pictures of polluted oceans for little kids; show the fix, not the disaster.

prompts.name: Helping the Earth for preschoolers

fields.description: Easy ways little kids can help the Earth, one per page: 1. Put paper in the recycling bin. 2. Rinse plastic bottles and recycle them. 3. Recycle glass jars. 4. Recycle metal cans. 5. Reuse a jar as a pencil holder. 6. Turn off the lights when you leave a room. 7. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. 8. Pick up litter at the park. 9. Plant a tree. 10. Put banana peels and apple cores in the compost. Show smiling kids and happy animals.

prompts.why: Pre-K teachers want an Earth Day book with ten simple actions a four-year-old can actually do, shown cheerfully. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Where does recycling go, ages 6-9

fields.description: After the recycling bin: 1. Reduce, reuse, recycle. 2. Sort paper, plastic, glass and metal. 3. The recycling truck collects the bins. 4. At the sorting center, machines separate everything. 5. Paper becomes pulp, then new paper. 6. Plastic bottles can become fleece jackets. 7. Aluminum cans can be recycled again and again. 8. Glass is melted into new jars. 9. Composting turns food scraps into soil. 10. Worms help compost. 11. Reusable bags and bottles. 12. Save water. 13. Save energy. 14. Earth Day is April 22.

prompts.why: Grade 1-3 teachers want to show the journey after the bin, which answers the question kids always ask: where does it go? Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Protecting our planet for ages 9-13

fields.description: Bigger ideas about caring for the planet: 1. What a landfill is. 2. Some materials take hundreds of years to break down. 3. How litter reaches rivers and the ocean. 4. Microplastics. 5. Composting returns nutrients to soil. 6. Upcycling old things into new ones. 7. Renewable energy: solar panels. 8. Wind turbines. 9. Saving electricity at home. 10. Saving water. 11. Trees take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen. 12. Protecting animal habitats. 13. A community cleanup. 14. Make an Earth Day pledge.

prompts.why: Upper elementary teachers need a science-based environment unit that ends on action, and homeschoolers get a full Earth Day week in one book. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Bees and Pollinators Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Bees and pollinators coloring book prompts for kids: how bees make honey, pollination, butterflies, bats and hummingbirds, one fact per page.
pages.intro: Bees and pollinators are a spring science favorite, and kids are amazed to learn that many fruits need an insect's visit to grow. These prompts cover a honeybee's day for preschoolers, the many kinds of pollinators for 6 to 9 year olds and life inside a honeybee colony for older kids. Every fact is short and true.
keywords: honey bee life cycle for kids
tips: Show the pollen on the bee's fuzzy body; it is the picture that makes pollination click for kids.
Include non-bee pollinators like bats, moths and hummingbirds; teachers love the surprise.
End with something kids can do, like planting flowers bees like.

prompts.name: A busy bee's day for preschoolers

fields.description: A honeybee's busy day, one idea per page: 1. A honeybee flies out of the hive in the morning. 2. She lands on a flower. 3. She sips sweet nectar. 4. Yellow pollen sticks to her fuzzy body. 5. She carries pollen to the next flower. 6. That helps the flower make seeds and fruit, like apples and strawberries. 7. She flies home to the hive. 8. Bees build honeycomb with six-sided cells. 9. Bees turn nectar into honey. 10. The queen bee lays eggs that grow into new bees.

prompts.why: Preschool teachers doing a spring insect unit want a friendly bee story with one clear idea per page, and it eases kids' fear of bees. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Pollinators and the food we eat

fields.description: Meet the pollinators and the foods they help grow: 1. What pollination is. 2. Honeybees. 3. Bumblebees can buzz pollen loose from tomato flowers. 4. Butterflies. 5. Moths visit flowers at night. 6. Hummingbirds drink nectar from tube-shaped flowers. 7. Some bats pollinate agave and banana flowers. 8. Beetles. 9. Flies. 10. Wind carries pollen for corn and grasses. 11. Apples, strawberries and pumpkins need pollinators. 12. Almonds need bees. 13. Plant a pollinator garden. 14. Leave clover and dandelions for the bees.

prompts.why: Grade 1-3 teachers love a pollinator unit that links insects to lunchbox food, and it makes a strong Earth Day or spring science book. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Inside the honeybee colony for ages 9-13

fields.description: Life inside a honeybee colony: 1. A colony has one queen, many workers and some drones. 2. The queen lays up to 1,500 eggs a day. 3. Egg. 4. Larva. 5. Pupa. 6. Adult bee. 7. Young workers clean cells. 8. Nurse bees feed larvae. 9. Builders make wax comb. 10. Guards protect the entrance. 11. Foragers collect nectar and pollen. 12. Pollen baskets on the back legs. 13. The waggle dance shows where flowers are. 14. Bees fan nectar to dry it into honey. 15. Solitary bees like mason bees. 16. Threats to bees and how to help.

prompts.why: Homeschoolers and middle-grade science teachers get a full honeybee biology unit, from metamorphosis to the waggle dance, in one book. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: Volcano and Earth Science Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: Volcano and earth science coloring book prompts for kids: how volcanoes erupt, Earth's layers, tectonic plates and the rock cycle, one idea per page.
pages.intro: Volcanoes are a gateway to earth science: once kids see magma rising, they want to know about Earth's layers, plates and rocks. These prompts start with a friendly volcano story for preschoolers and build to tectonic plates and the full rock cycle for 9 to 13 year olds. Each page explains one idea with a clear cutaway drawing.
keywords: layers of the earth coloring page
tips: Ask for cutaway views on key pages so kids can see the magma chamber and Earth's layers inside.
Teach magma versus lava early: it is magma underground and lava once it comes out.
Finish with rocks kids can find, like pumice or granite, so the book connects to a nature walk.

prompts.name: Volcanoes for little learners

fields.description: A first volcano book, one idea per page: 1. A volcano is a mountain with an opening at the top. 2. Deep under the ground it is very hot. 3. The heat melts rock into magma. 4. Magma rises up inside the volcano. 5. When the volcano erupts, the magma comes out and is called lava. 6. Clouds of ash puff into the sky. 7. Lava cools down and turns into new rock. 8. Some volcanoes make new islands in the sea. 9. Scientists called volcanologists study volcanoes safely. 10. After a long time, plants grow back on the volcano.

prompts.why: Volcano-loving preschoolers get real science in tiny steps, and parents like a book that explains the eruption without anything frightening. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Earth's layers and volcanoes for ages 6-9

fields.description: Inside the Earth: 1. The crust is the thin layer we live on. 2. The mantle is hot, slowly moving rock. 3. The outer core is liquid metal. 4. The inner core is solid metal. 5. The crust is broken into tectonic plates. 6. Plates moving cause earthquakes. 7. The Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean. 8. Magma vs lava. 9. Shield volcanoes have gentle slopes. 10. Stratovolcanoes are tall and steep. 11. Cinder cones are small. 12. Pumice is so full of air it floats. 13. Obsidian is natural volcanic glass. 14. Geysers shoot hot water up.

prompts.why: Grade 2-3 teachers covering Earth's structure want each layer and volcano type on its own page, and the floating pumice fact always gets a reaction. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Rocks and the rock cycle for ages 9-13

fields.description: The rock cycle: 1. Rocks are made of minerals. 2. Igneous rock forms when magma or lava cools. 3. Granite cools slowly underground. 4. Basalt cools fast at the surface. 5. Weathering breaks rock apart. 6. Water, wind and ice carry sediment away. 7. Sediment settles in layers. 8. Layers press into sedimentary rock like sandstone. 9. Fossils hide in sedimentary rock. 10. Heat and pressure make metamorphic rock. 11. Limestone becomes marble. 12. Shale becomes slate. 13. Rock melts back into magma. 14. The Mohs scale: talc is 1, diamond is 10.

prompts.why: Upper elementary earth science always includes the rock cycle, and a labeled page per stage gives homeschoolers and teachers a ready study guide. Its short length is great for home printing.

pages.title: World Cultures and Landmarks Coloring Book Prompts for Kids
pages.metaDescription: World cultures coloring book prompts for kids: hello in many languages, famous world landmarks and festivals around the world, respectful and factual.
pages.intro: A world cultures coloring book helps kids see how big and varied the world is, from saying hello in Swahili to lighting lamps for Diwali. These prompts cover greetings for preschoolers, famous landmarks for 6 to 9 year olds and festivals around the world for older kids. Each brief asks for respectful, everyday, modern pictures of people and places, never costumes or stereotypes.
keywords: festivals around the world for kids
tips: Ask for people in everyday modern clothes at home, school or a market; traditional dress only where the occasion calls for it, like a festival.
Name the country and a true fact on every page, so the book teaches geography as well as culture.
Check spellings of greetings and festival names in the brief; they appear in the captions.

prompts.name: Hello around the world for preschoolers

fields.description: Saying hello around the world, one child and one greeting per page, with an animal or place from that country: 1. Hola, Mexico (monarch butterflies). 2. Bonjour, France (Eiffel Tower). 3. Jambo, Kenya (giraffe). 4. Konnichiwa, Japan (cherry blossoms). 5. Namaste, India (peacock). 6. Ni hao, China (panda). 7. Ciao, Italy (Leaning Tower of Pisa). 8. Marhaba, Egypt (pyramids). 9. Olá, Brazil (toucan). 10. Kia ora, New Zealand (kiwi bird). 11. Annyeonghaseyo, South Korea (hanok house). 12. Hello, Canada (moose). Children in everyday modern clothes, smiling and waving, never in costume.

prompts.why: Preschool teachers building a multicultural classroom want a gentle first look at other languages, and kids love saying each hello out loud. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Famous landmarks of the world for ages 6-9

fields.description: Famous landmarks with one fact each: 1. Great Wall of China, thousands of miles long. 2. Pyramids of Giza, Egypt, over 4,500 years old. 3. Eiffel Tower, Paris. 4. Taj Mahal, India, white marble. 5. Machu Picchu, Peru, high in the Andes. 6. Statue of Liberty, New York. 7. Great Barrier Reef, Australia, seen from space. 8. Colosseum, Rome. 9. Petra, Jordan, carved into rock. 10. Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. 11. Angkor Wat, Cambodia. 12. Chichen Itza, Mexico. 13. Stonehenge, England. 14. Iguazu Falls, on the border of Brazil and Argentina.

prompts.why: Teachers and homeschoolers use landmarks to anchor geography, and one landmark per page with a fact makes a map unit hands-on. Its short length is great for home printing.

prompts.name: Festivals around the world for ages 9-13

fields.description: Festivals, shown respectfully with families taking part: 1. Diwali, lamps and rangoli. 2. Lunar New Year, lion dance and red envelopes. 3. Holi, colored powder in spring. 4. Eid al-Fitr ends Ramadan with a family meal. 5. Hanukkah, the menorah's eight nights. 6. Christmas, Jesus's birth, a decorated tree. 7. Kwanzaa, the kinara. 8. Day of the Dead, marigolds for loved ones. 9. Carnival in Brazil, kids parading with drums and confetti. 10. Songkran, Thai New Year. 11. Nowruz, Persian New Year. 12. Mid-Autumn Festival, mooncakes. 13. Inti Raymi, Peru. 14. Homowo, Ghana, a harvest feast.

prompts.why: Teachers building an inclusive classroom want festivals from many faiths and countries treated equally and accurately, one per page. Its short length is great for home printing.
